title: fix: prevent multi-diff phantom headers while scrolling
body:
## Summary
- Multi-diff virtualization deferred hiding off-screen row templates until an autorun ran, so during fast scroll the old DOM stayed visible and produced repeated/sliver headers (#326702).
- `VirtualizedViewItem.hide()` now immediately hides the template DOM and synchronously returns unfocused templates to the object pool.
- Recycled templates seed content height from the target view model's `lastTemplateData`, and `ObjectPool` drops `_itemData` when disposing overflow objects.
- Adds unit tests for `ObjectPool` reuse / id preference / overflow dispose.

Fixes #326702

## Test plan
- [x] Unit: `ObjectPool` suite (3 tests) via `test/unit/electron/index.js --grep ObjectPool`
- [ ] Manual: open a multi-diff with ~30+ files (`vscode.changes` / SCM Open All Changes), scroll aggressively up/down; headers should stay 1:1 with files (no repeated phantom headers at ~35px)
- [ ] Manual: focused nested diff editor is not torn down while its row is scrolled off (still deferred recycle when focused)

title: Chat dictation: always use Nemotron model, remove model setting
body:
The on-device chat dictation runtime is Microsoft Foundry Local's streaming ASR engine, and the only supported model is NVIDIA Nemotron (`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b` — the model the GitHub Copilot app ships). The `chat.speechToText.model` setting therefore only ever had a single valid value, and the legacy Whisper model IDs no longer resolve.

This PR removes model selection entirely and hardcodes Nemotron:

- **Remove the `chat.speechToText.model` setting.** Its migration is replaced with one that clears any explicitly-stored value so it doesn't linger as an unknown setting (this also drops the legacy `onnx-community/whisper-*` references).
- **`ChatSpeechToTextService`**: remove `MODEL_SETTING` and `_getModelId()`; start the local session without a model argument.
- **`ILocalTranscriptionService.start()`**: drop the unused optional `model` option from the interface, the electron-browser proxy, and the node implementation. The node service always uses the Nemotron default.

No user-facing behavior change: dictation already defaulted to Nemotron. This just removes the dead selection surface and the last Whisper references.

### Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.

title: [cherry-pick] Add telemetry for applied enterprise policies

labels.name: cherry-pick-artifact
labels.description: Auto-generated cherry-pick PR

body:
Cherry-pick of #326686 from `main`.

## Summary

Adds a consolidated `policy.applied` telemetry event for understanding enterprise policy adoption.

The event:

- Fires once after workbench restoration and again when effective policy state changes.
- Debounces change bursts by 500 ms and suppresses duplicate payloads.
- Reports the total number of applied policies.
- Reports whether selected chat, plugin, OpenTelemetry, telemetry-level, and feedback policies are applied.
- Reports low-cardinality value buckets for default-model auto selection, tool auto-approval being forced off, marketplace lockdown, OTel being forced on, and telemetry level.
- Never reports raw policy values, model identifiers, organization names, plugin IDs, marketplace URLs, or other user/admin-provided strings.

The contribution reads only authoritative effective values from `IPolicyService`. Delivery-source attribution is intentionally excluded because the current policy service API does not expose which child of `MultiplexPolicyService` supplied the winning value.

Supersedes #325385, preserving Harald's original commit and simplifying the implementation from five changed files to three.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/policyTelemetryContribution.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- VS Code hygiene checks
- `@vscode/telemetry-extractor@1.14.0`

Focused tests cover the empty startup event, every reported policy and value bucket, privacy-safe handling of unexpected values, the total applied-policy count, debounced updates, and payload deduplication.

title: Copilot Chat: Confusing error when BYOK utility model not configured
body:
﻿## Issue
When using a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) model as the main agent model in VS Code Copilot Chat, switching to Agent mode fails with:
```
No utility model is configured for 'copilot-utility-small' while the selected main agent model is BYOK.
```

This error is confusing because:
1. It doesn't tell the user HOW to configure a utility model
2. It doesn't mention the `chat.byokUtilityModelDefault` setting that can solve this
3. The error persists even after clearing extension cache (because it's a settings issue, not a cache issue)

## Environment
- **VS Code Version**: 1.106+ (current stable)
- **Copilot Extension**: Latest version
- **OS**: Windows 11
- **Model Setup**: BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) configuration

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a repository with Copilot Chat enabled
2. Configure a BYOK model as your main agent model (not Copilot's hosted models)
3. Do NOT configure `chat.utilitySmallModel` or `chat.byokUtilityModelDefault` settings
4. Switch from "Ask" mode to "Agent" mode in the chat panel
5. Error appears immediately

## Expected Behavior
The error message should be actionable and tell the user:
- Which settings to configure (`chat.utilitySmallModel` or `chat.byokUtilityModelDefault`)
- That setting `chat.byokUtilityModelDefault` to `'mainAgent'` will use their BYOK model for utility tasks
- This is a configuration requirement, not a bug

## Root Cause
From `extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompt/vscode-node/endpointProviderImpl.ts`:

The error IS created with helpful text, but it may not be surfacing to the user properly in the UI.

## Solution for Users
Add this to VS Code settings (User or Workspace):

**Option 1: Use your BYOK model for utility tasks (recommended)**
```json
{
    "chat.byokUtilityModelDefault": "mainAgent"
}
```

**Option 2: Specify a specific utility model**
```json
{
    "chat.utilitySmallModel": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5"
}
```

## Impact
Medium - prevents use of Agent mode for code generation, file editing, and terminal operations in BYOK setups, but has a straightforward fix.

**Suggested Fix:** Surface the full error message to the user in the UI, or show a notification/banner with the configuration guidance when this error occurs.

title: Audit Copilot SDK events with agentId for subagent-safe handling

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

milestone.title: On Deck
milestone.description: The Issues assigned to the **On Deck** milestone under consideration for the upcoming milestones.

body:
## Context

Copilot SDK session event envelopes can carry an optional `agentId` when emitted for a subagent. We hardened `user.message` handling so subagent messages do not mutate root steering/event-ID state or emit root-only instruction telemetry, and replay restores them in the subagent transcript.

The SDK exposes `agentId` across its event union. Audit the remaining Agent Host consumers for root-only assumptions and either route, ignore, or explicitly document each subagent event.

## Events to review

Highest-risk state-mutating consumers:

- `system.notification`: currently creates or appends root turns in live handling and replay.
- `session.idle`: currently completes or aborts the root turn.
- `session.error`: currently emits a root chat error.
- `session.auto_mode_resolved`: currently updates root model and usage state.
- `assistant.intent`: currently updates root session activity.
- `session.model_change`: currently affects root replay model selection.
- `assistant.usage`: an unmapped subagent event can currently fall back to root usage.
- MCP server, tool, and command inventory events: currently treated as session-global; verify whether subagent-scoped variants should be ignored or projected globally.

Logging-only and memo-invalidation listeners do not need guards unless their behavior gains stateful side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- Classify every consumed SDK event that may carry `agentId` as session-global, root-only, or subagent-routed.
- Add explicit guards or routing for root-only and subagent-scoped behavior.
- Drop and warn for unmapped subagent events where ordering/correlation is required.
- Keep live handling and persisted-history replay behavior consistent.
- Add focused regression tests for each state-mutating path changed.

(Written by Copilot)

title: JSON - support ${workspaceFolder} in json.schemas fileMatch patterns
body:
Fixes #44135

Implements the approach from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/44135#issuecomment-5022741898: `${workspaceFolder}` is expanded on the client, and the server API stays unchanged.

### Change

- `jsonClient.ts`: when collecting `json.schemas` settings, a leading `${workspaceFolder}` in a `fileMatch` pattern (also after a `!` exclusion prefix) expands to the workspace folder path. This happens in the two scopes with an unambiguous folder: workspace folder settings in a multi-root workspace, and workspace settings of a single-folder workspace. User settings and multi-root workspace-file settings are left untouched (no single folder to expand to). Non-array/non-string values pass through unchanged.
- `utils/strings.ts`: `escapeGlobCharacters`, used to insert the folder path into the pattern.
- `package.nls.json`: documents the new pattern form.

Since the expanded pattern carries the folder path, the server's implicit `**/` prefix no longer widens it below the folder — `${workspaceFolder}/*.json` matches only in the folder root, `${workspaceFolder}/sub/*.json` only in that subfolder, and existing patterns behave exactly as before.

### Validation

- A parity harness against the service's real `createRegex` + `vscode-uri` (66 cases): root-only and subfolder anchoring, recursive `**` patterns, exclusions, the multi-root `folderUri` gate, folder names with spaces/unicode/parens/`$`/glob metacharacters/`#`/`?`, uppercase drive letters, filesystem-root and drive-root folders, and malformed `fileMatch` values (bare string, non-string entries — no throw, pass through).
- End-to-end in a dev build, re-run on this revision: with a `${workspaceFolder}/*.json` schema and a plain `*.json` schema both requiring a property, the folder-root file reports two diagnostics and a file in a subfolder reports one — the anchored schema applies at the root only.

### Notes

- The folder path is spelled the way the server spells the document uris it matches against: a leading drive letter is lowercased and `#` and `?` are percent-encoded — `Uri.path` lowercases neither and decodes both. Glob metacharacters are encoded as `\xAB` escapes, which the glob parser copies through to the generated regular expression, so folder names like `my[proj]` or `w*s` match literally. A backslash escape can't be used for this — the parser has no escape syntax, so it copies the backslash through and still reads the next character as glob syntax.
- Being a path, the pattern is not tied to a scheme or authority, and the `**/` prefix still allows leading segments before it — the same as any absolute pattern written by hand today. In a multi-root workspace the existing `folderUri` gate still scopes each pattern to its folder.
- While validating the multi-root case I noticed folder-scoped `json.schemas` (in a folder's `.vscode/settings.json` inside a `.code-workspace`) don't reach the server even for plain patterns, also on stable 1.129 — that looks like a separate pre-existing issue, independent of this change. I can file it with the minimal fixture if useful.

body: Type: Bug VS Code version: 1.129.0 and 1.129.1 (both affected) OS version: macOS 15.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon, external 4K display (BenQ EW3270U) ### Summary The multi-diff editor (opened via the `vscode.changes` command) intermittently corrupts its virtualized rows **after scrolling** a diff with ~30+ resources: many rows render with the **same file header repeated** (one file's basename/dirname/status badge shown 10–20 times) at sliver heights (~35 px), interleaved with thin slices of *other* files' content. Which file becomes the "phantom" repeated header **changes with scroll position**. Clicking into / settling on a row renders that file perfectly; closing and reopening the multi-diff editor always clears the corruption. ### Steps to reproduce 1. An extension opens a multi-diff via `vscode.changes` with ~35 triples `[label, original, modified]` whose sides are URIs of a registered `TextDocumentContentProvider` (custom scheme; every document resolves promptly and correctly — initial render is clean and fully expanded). 2. Scroll up and down through the multi-diff for a while (mouse wheel, varying speed). 3. Observe rows collapsing into repeated phantom headers of a single file with sliver-height content slices from unrelated files. Synthetic content generator we used (any repo shape with ~35 modified/added/deleted files of a few hundred lines reproduces the input): ```bash mkdir soup-repo && cd soup-repo && git init -q for i in $(seq 1 35); do mkdir -p "mod$((i%7))"; { echo "# module $i"; for l in $(seq 1 220); do echo "function fn_${i}_${l}() { return ${l}; } // line ${l}"; done; } > "mod$((i%7))/file_$i.js"; done git add -A && git commit -qm base for i in $(seq 1 30); do f="mod$((i%7))/file_$i.js"; sed -i '' "s/return 5;/return 500;/" $f; echo "// appended $i" >> $f; done for i in 31 32; do rm "mod$((i%7))/file_$i.js"; done for i in 36 37 38; do echo "// new $i" > "mod$((i%7))/new_$i.js"; done git add -A && git commit -qm head ``` then, in an extension host, open triples built from `git diff --name-status -z HEAD~1 HEAD` (original = `HEAD~1` side, modified = `HEAD` side, `undefined` sides for A/D) via `vscode.commands.executeCommand("vscode.changes", title, triples)`. ### Observations - Reproduced on two different days (1.129.0, then 1.129.1 after updating) in a long-lived window; both times only **after scrolling** — the initial render is always correct. - A fresh instance (`@vscode/test-electron`, only our development extension loaded) given the identical 32-file input rendered cleanly at open; title: Omni-chat with multi-session routing
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8461

Addresses #329698

## What

Adds a floating, frameless, always-on-top Omni Chat input that hosts the compact `ChatWidget`, including multiline editing, attachments, model/mode selection, dictation, Voice Mode, and input glow.

Toggle it with **Toggle Floating Chat Input Window** (`workbench.action.chat.toggleInputWindow`).

## Session routing

Omni submissions do not run in the input window's scratch session. `ChatSessionRoutingController` instead:

1. Collects active Copilot agent sessions, excluding Omni's scratch session and read-only or archived sessions.
2. Scores every candidate semantically, then enriches a bounded shortlist with clipped conversation history.
3. Uses the utility language model to select the most relevant session, with lexical scoring only as a deterministic tie-breaker.
4. Starts a new Copilot session when no existing session is a confident match or the user explicitly requests a new session.
5. In multi-root workspaces, determines the destination folder for a new session in this order:
   - **Attached resource:** the workspace folder containing the first attached file or resource that maps to the workspace.
   - **Explicit folder mention:** a case-insensitive, whole-name match against a workspace folder's display name or final path segment. Names shorter than three characters are ignored, and the longest matching name wins.
   - **Related session:** the first model-ranked result with confidence of at least 0.35 whose metadata maps to a workspace folder. The session's working directory is checked before its repository path; nested workspace matches prefer the deepest folder.
   - **Default:** the last folder selected for a new Agent Host session, when it is still part of the workspace.
   - **Final fallback:** the first workspace folder.

The resolved folder is shown in the proposed **New session in _folder_** destination. In a multi-root workspace, **Change Folder** lets the user override it before dispatch.

Before dispatch, Omni presents a correctable destination list:

- **Arrow keys** move between destinations.
- **Space** toggles destinations for fan-out.
- **Enter** sends to the selected destination(s).
- **Escape** cancels.
- Continuing to edit the prompt or attachments cancels the pending route.

Existing Agent Host routes preserve their session-owned model. New sessions use the model selected in Omni. Queued requests retain their session reference until delivery and distinguish sent, cancelled, removed, and failed outcomes.

Routing metadata and transcripts are scoped to Copilot providers; sessions owned by other providers are not sent to the Copilot router.

## Voice Mode

Voice Mode has explicit surface ownership:

- Omni owns capture, draft state, routed target, and active window as one transfer.
- A single route pins Voice Mode to the actual destination session.
- Fan-out clears the sticky target rather than selecting an arbitrary session.
- The hold-to-barge-in keybinding preserves an Omni-owned target when invoked in Omni, while invoking it from panel chat intentionally transfers ownership to panel chat.
- Closing, blurring after a completed turn, or disconnecting releases Omni ownership and stale routing state.

Pending questions and approvals from routed sessions are surfaced in Omni. Terminal approvals show the exact command plus approval message, disclaimer/risk explanation, custom choices, and reliable **Allow Once**/**Skip** controls. Resolved approvals retain semantic tombstones so rehydrated tool cards cannot become actionable again.

## Window behavior

- The leading grip moves the frameless window; Send and Close remain independent controls.
- The auxiliary window grows for multiline input, destination choices, pending questions, and approvals.
- Long approval content is bounded and scrollable.
- Model-picker expansion restores the previous fitted height without stealing focus after an asynchronous resize.
- The floating surface is hidden when AI features are disabled or Chat entitlement is hidden.

## Implementation

- `chat/common/sessionRouter.ts` defines the routing contract and parser.
- `chat/browser/sessionRouter/` owns candidate collection, history enrichment, ranking, folder selection, dispatch, queue lifecycle, and delivery feedback.
- `chat/browser/chatInputWindow/` owns the auxiliary surface, compact widget, routing host, pending-input UI, and sizing.
- `chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceSessionController.ts` owns atomic Voice Mode surface/target transfer, routed narration, and approval identity.
- Shared auxiliary-window bounds APIs keep browser-layer code independent of Electron-only native services.

## Validation

- Client compilation and layer checks
- Focused routing, Voice Mode, approval-identity, and routing-helper suites in Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox
- Manual testing of existing/new-session routing, multi-root folder choice, Voice Mode barge-in ownership, terminal approvals, custom approval options, long content, and multiple pending sessions

## Description

Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+I did nothing in the Agents window chat composer, while it worked in the main window chat input.

**Root cause:** the Agents composer (`NewChatInputWidget`) handled the dictation chord via a raw editor `onKeyDown` listener. That path loses the chord to `editor.action.triggerSuggest`, which binds Cmd/Ctrl+I as a secondary keybinding at `EditorContrib` weight. The main window works because it registers dictation through the keybinding service at `WorkbenchContrib + 1`, outranking Trigger Suggest.

**Changes** (`src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/newChatInput.ts`):

- Register `sessions.action.chat.toggleDictation` (Cmd/Ctrl+I) through the keybinding service at `WorkbenchContrib + 1`, gated on a new `sessionsChatInputHasDictationFocus` context key and `chatSpeechToTextConfigured` — so it reliably wins the chord, and falls back to Trigger Suggest when dictation isn't available.
- Track the focused composer at module scope and route the command to it (the composer isn't an `IChatWidget`, so the shared Dictate action can't reach it); cleared on blur/dispose.
- Remove the fragile `onKeyDown` Cmd/Ctrl+I branch; expose a public `toggleDictation()`.

```ts
KeybindingsRegistry.registerCommandAndKeybindingRule({
	id: 'sessions.action.chat.toggleDictation',
	weight: KeybindingWeight.WorkbenchContrib + 1,
	when: ContextKeyExpr.and(
		SessionsChatInputHasDictationFocus,
		ContextKeyExpr.has(ChatContextKeys.speechToTextConfigured.key),

	primary: KeyMod.CtrlCmd | KeyCode.KeyI,
```

title: Voice: clear routing/pending state on disconnect and remove idle glow
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8515

## Voice: clear routing/pending state on disconnect

`VoiceSessionController.disconnect()` (and `_handleFatalDisconnect`) reset most state but never cleared the user-picked routing target (`_targetSession`) or the always-on pending-confirmation snapshot (`_pendingToolConfirmations`).

Because `_targetSession` survived teardown, reconnecting from a different, newly focused session re-pinned voice to the *previously* targeted session:

- the previous session's input glow/mic indicator lit up again, and
- the next utterance was routed to it (sent as a plain follow-up request) instead of resolving its pending confirmation.

Both terminal-teardown paths now reset `_targetSession` and `_pendingToolConfirmations`, so a later `connect()` starts from focus-based detection.

### Repro (before)
1. Create a voice session ("Create a new file").
2. While it's working, disconnect voice → session shows "input needed".
3. Create a new session and reactivate voice.
4. The mic indicator reappears on the old session and voice is re-pinned there; saying "approve it" skips the question and is sent as a follow-up.

## Remove the connected-idle glow

Removes the white/themed "breathing" idle glow from voice mode in both the main window (`ChatViewPane`) and the Agents window (`agentsVoiceWidget` / `voiceInputDecorations`). Voice mode now only glows while **listening** or **speaking**.

- `voiceGlow.ts` drops the idle intensity/color/branch and exposes `isGlowingVoiceState()` so callers gate their animation loops consistently.
- Removes the now-dead `.voice-idle` CSS rules and the unused `isMotionReduced` glow plumbing.
- Updates `voiceGlow.test.ts` accordingly.

Summary
- Client-provided tools could still show a confirmation prompt in Allow All or Assisted Permissions mode, even though Agent Host had already approved the invocation.

Root Cause
- Agent Host represented the approval using the protocol’s confirmed field, commonly as not-needed. The client tool bridge only recognized the separate autoApproveBySetting metadata flag, so it invoked the local tool without passing through the existing approval.

The local tool service consequently performed its own confirmation flow.

- Continue supporting the existing autoApproveBySetting metadata path.
- Pass the resolved approval into local client-tool invocation.
- Apply late-arriving approval state if an invocation is already waiting for confirmation.

title: Dictation: migrate on-device runtime to Foundry Local streaming ASR
body:
Vastly improves latency and accuracy of dictation

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d35dcb2f-e3b1-4a65-b728-e37f43efdd3e

## What & why

The GitHub Copilot app's on-device dictation feels snappier and more accurate than VS Code's. It runs through **Microsoft Foundry Local**'s native streaming ASR runtime (onnxruntime + onnxruntime-genai), which does decode, VAD and endpointing in native code, using NVIDIA's `nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b` streaming RNN-T model.

This draft replaces VS Code's dictation pipeline (transformers.js Whisper + a hand-rolled Nemotron RNN-T decoder on `onnxruntime-node`) with the same **Foundry Local** engine for parity.

## Changes

- **Node service rewrite** (`platform/localTranscription/node/localTranscriptionService.ts`): drives `foundry-local-sdk` — async `FoundryLocalManager`, model download/load progress, a live streaming session. Buffers captured PCM until the session opens (so first-use download doesn't drop leading audio), then streams raw PCM16; accumulates a cumulative transcript from per-segment `is_final` results and emits interim/final transcripts.
- **Deleted** `nemotronTranscriber.ts` (native decode now lives in Foundry).
- **Setting**: `chat.speechToText.model` enum → Foundry model alias (`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`, default).
- **Interface/proxy docs** updated to Foundry Local; platform gate kept (its `SUPPORTED_TARGETS` already match Foundry's prebuild targets exactly: darwin-arm64, linux-x64/arm64, win32-x64/arm64).
- **Packaging**: bundle `foundry-local-sdk` native addon + core libs (gulpfile ASAR-unpack + per-target prebuild filter, darwin macho/universal, linux dep scanner) in place of `onnxruntime-node`. Dropped `@huggingface/transformers`, `onnxruntime-node`, and the `sharp` stub.

## Description

The on-device dictation transcript (`_finalizedText`/`_deltaText`) was cleared inconsistently across `ChatSpeechToTextService` session lifecycles: on `cancel()` and `_failSession()`, and on the *next* `start()` — but only *after* the async microphone-acquisition prompt. A normal `stopAndTranscribe()` ("Stop recording") left the prior transcript in service state, so a subsequent recording could resurface it.

Changes:

- **Centralize the reset in `_teardown()`** — every session-end path (stop, cancel, error, and `start()`'s error paths) already funnels through here, so the transcript is now cleared the instant a session ends rather than on the next start. This removes the window in which stale text could reappear.
- **Remove the now-redundant resets** in `start()`, `cancel()`, and `_failSession()`, making `_teardown()` the single source of truth for the invariant "no transcript survives the session that produced it."

The returned final transcript is captured in a local and telemetry (`transcriptLength`) is logged *before* `_teardown()`, so both remain correct.

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.107.1
- OS Version: Windows 10/11 (x64) with WSL installed

## Bug Description

`getWslProfiles()` in `src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProfiles.ts` calls `cp.exec("wsl.exe -l -q")` synchronously on the main thread (CrBrowserMain / Node.js event loop). On Windows, `uv_spawn` → `CreateProcessW` → `NtCreateUserProcess` is a **blocking kernel call** that can stall the main thread for **100ms to 6+ seconds**, causing full UI freeze.

## Root Cause

The `cp.exec("wsl.exe -l -q")` call in `getWslProfiles` (terminalProfiles.ts:347-358) executes on the main thread. On Windows, libuv's `uv_spawn` invokes `CreateProcessW` which is a synchronous kernel call — the `timeout: 1000` option only limits stdout wait time, **not** the process creation itself.

`wsl.exe` is particularly slow to spawn because:
1. WSL subsystem cold-start may require launching a lightweight VM / Hyper-V instance
2. Antivirus software (Windows Defender, etc.) hooks and scans `CreateProcess`
3. Kernel resource contention under high system load

## Call Stack (native + JS, sourcemap-resolved)
- native call stack
[crash_stack (1).txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30196545/crash_stack.1.txt)
- node js call stack
```
at getWslProfiles (lib/vscode/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProfiles.ts:151:24)
    const result = await getWslProfiles(`${system32Path}\\wsl.exe`, defaultProfileName);
at ube (lib/vscode/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProfiles.ts:349:28)
    const distroOutput = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => 
at new Promise (<anonymous>)
at r (lib/vscode/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProfiles.ts:352:5)
    cp.exec('wsl.exe -l -q', { encoding: 'utf16le', env: { ...process.env, WSL_UTF8: '0' }, timeout: 1000 }, (err, stdout) => 
at Module.exec (node:child_process:236:25)
at t.<computed> [as execFile] (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:3013)
at Object.execFile (node:child_process:349:17)
at spawn (node:child_process:801:9)
at ChildProcess.spawn (node:internal/child_process:422:13)
at process.nextTick (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:149394)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use VS Code on Windows with WSL installed (especially with multiple distros).
2. Open VS Code — terminal profile detection runs automatically on startup.
3. Open the terminal dropdown or create a new terminal instance.
4. Observe UI freeze/jank for 100ms~seconds while `wsl.exe -l -q` spawns.
5. Reproduction is more reliable when: WSL has not been used recently (cold start), antivirus is active, or system is under load.

## Expected Behavior

Terminal profile detection should not block the main thread. The UI should remain responsive during WSL profile enumeration.

title: Prompt to disable redundant VS Code Speech extension when built-in dictation is available
body:
## Summary

Adds a one-time notification suggesting users disable the [`ms-vscode.vscode-speech`](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode.vscode-speech) extension once VS Code's built-in on-device chat dictation makes it redundant.

New workbench contribution `RedundantDictationExtensionNotifier` (registered at `WorkbenchPhase.Eventually`) shows the prompt **only when all** of the following hold:

1. **Platform supports built-in dictation** — `ILocalTranscriptionService.isSupported`, the same predicate that shows/hides the built-in mic button (false on macOS Intel, unsupported Linux archs, web, remote — no new platform logic).
2. **Built-in dictation is enabled** — `chat.speechToText.enabled === true`, so we never suggest disabling a working extension before its replacement is turned on.
3. **Extension installed & enabled** — via `IExtensionsWorkbenchService.queryLocal()` + positive `enablementState` check.
4. **Never shown before** — application-scoped `IStorageService` flag, set the moment the prompt appears, so it fires at most once ever regardless of the user's choice.

### Prompt

> VS Code now has built-in dictation, so the 'VS Code Speech' extension is no longer needed. Disable it?

- **Disable Extension** → `setEnablement(ext, EnablementState.DisabledGlobally)`
- **Keep** → dismiss

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors.
- Manual: on a supported platform with the extension installed and `chat.speechToText.enabled` on, the prompt appears once; choosing *Disable Extension* disables it; the prompt does not reappear after restart.

### Summary `TreeError [SearchView] Tree element not found` is thrown when a user moves a Quick Search (Go to File / text search quick access) result into the full Search view via the "Open in Search View" / "More" / "See More Files" affordances. `TextSearchQuickAccess.moveToSearchViewlet` transfers its search model to the Search view and then calls `viewer.setSelection([currentElem])` on the view's `WorkbenchCompressibleAsyncDataTree`. Because that tree lazy-loads its nodes, `currentElem` (often a deep `Match` under a not-yet-expanded file, or a file match beyond the visible limit) may not be materialized in the tree yet, so `setSelection` throws. The impact is an unhandled error surfaced to telemetry and a failed "open in search view" gesture. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326646 Recommended reviewer: `@osortega` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`88056f2`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/88056f2c97d6bde7cf151bfff35b4c3e2c65b407) | | Author | `@andreamah` | | PR | #228886 | | Message | Use `WorkbenchCompressibleAsyncDataTree` for lazy loading AI results (#228886) | | Why | This commit converted the Search view tree from a fully-materialized sync tree to a lazy-loading async data tree. `moveToSearchViewlet` kept calling `setSelection`/`reveal` with an element reference that a sync tree always contained but the async tree only contains once its parent chain has been loaded, so the pre-existing call became able to throw `Tree element not found`. | > This is a long-standing mechanism (the async-tree conversion predates the shipped build by well over a year) surfaced as a recent telemetry spike, so it is effectively pre-existing; `88056f2` is named because it is the change that made the `setSelection` call unsafe. The fix is independent of exact culprit attribution. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as Quick Search pick participant QA as TextSearchQuickAccess.moveToSearchViewlet participant View as SearchView.replaceSearchModel participant Tree as CompressibleAsyncDataTree participant Model as CompressedObjectTreeModel User->>QA: accept "Open in Search View" / "More" QA->>View: replaceSearchModel(model) (queues async refresh) Note over View: setInput + queued updateChildren;
deep nodes not yet materialized QA->>Tree: setSelection([currentElem]) Tree->>Model: map element -> node (getNode/getCompressedNode) Note over Model: ⚠️ element not in nodes map Note over Model: 💥 TreeError [SearchView] Tree element not found ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/compressedObjectTreeModel.ts` | crash site | L347 `throw new TreeError(this.user, 'Tree element not found: ...')` (from stack) | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/browser/quickTextSearch/textSearchQuickAccess.ts` | root cause | L219-L226: `viewer.setSelection([currentElem])` called on a lazy async tree with an element (`matches[limit]` L256 / deep `element` L291) that may not be materialized | | `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts` | precondition | L839-L850 `hasNode()` reports whether an element has been materialized in the async tree | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a folder with many text matches for a common term. 2. Open Quick Search (text search quick access) and type a term producing many results, enough to show the "More" / "See More Files" separators. 3. Trigger "Open in Search View" / "More" on a match whose file match is not expanded/loaded (or a file match beyond the shown limit). 4. Intermittently, the transferred Search view tree has not yet materialized that node, so `setSelection` throws `TreeError [SearchView] Tree element not found`. Timing-dependent: larger result sets and collapsed files increase the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `textSearchQuickAccess.ts` → `moveToSearchViewlet()`: guard the `setFocus`/`setSelection`/`reveal` block on `viewer?.hasNode(currentElem)`. When the element has not been materialized in the async tree, fall back to focusing the search widget — the exact behavior the existing `else` branch already provides for the "no element" case. This checks a documented precondition of the async-data-tree API before invoking it, at the site that produces the invalid call (fix at the caller that makes the unsupported call, not at the shared tree crash site). It reuses the same `hasNode` materialization check already used elsewhere in this view (`RefreshTreeController.refreshTree`, `searchView.ts` L2769), so it introduces no new contract and no `try/catch` that would hide errors from telemetry. **Lifecycle pattern**: async-init race (stale/unmaterialized cached reference) — the consumer holds a `RenderableMatch` that the freshly-input async tree has not yet loaded. **Producer site**: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/browser/searchView.ts:469` — `replaceSearchModel` calls `setInput` and only queues (does not synchronously complete) the tree refresh, so deep nodes are absent when control returns to the caller. **Why this fix**: after this change, `textSearchQuickAccess.ts:220` only calls `setSelection`/`reveal` when `hasNode` confirms the element exists, so `CompressedObjectTreeModel.getCompressedNode` can no longer receive an absent element from this path. **Alternatives considered**: awaiting a full recursive tree materialization/`expandTo` inside `replaceSearchModel` before returning — rejected because it would force-expand collapsed file matches (changing UX) and broaden the change well beyond the failing path for a gesture whose graceful degradation (focus the widget) already exists. ### Recommended Owner `@osortega` — current Search View owner per `microsoft/vscode-engineering` `triage/working-areas.md` (the culprit-commit author's change is effectively pre-existing; title: fix: register LM tools extension point handler at BlockStartup (fixes #326643)
body:
### Summary `unhandlederror-Tool "renderMermaidDiagram" was not contributed.` is thrown on the main thread when an extension registers a language-model **tool implementation** (via `vscode.lm.registerTool(id, ...)`) before the matching **tool data** from that extension's `package.json` `languageModelTools` contribution has been registered. The tool data is registered by the `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler` workbench contribution. It was registered at `WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore` (`LifecyclePhase.Ready`), whereas the sibling `ChatExtensionPointHandler` — which registers chat participant contributions the same way — runs at `WorkbenchPhase.BlockStartup` (`LifecyclePhase.Starting`). Because extensions can begin activating around the `Ready` phase, the tools extension-point handler's `setHandler` had not necessarily installed (and replayed the contributed tool data) before an extension activated and called `$registerTool`. On the main thread `registerToolImplementation` then finds no entry in `_tools` for the id and throws `Tool "" was not contributed.`. `renderMermaidDiagram` (contributed by the built-in `mermaid-markdown-features` extension) is the observed trigger: the extension activates through non-tool paths (e.g. `extendMarkdownIt` / webview-panel restore) and unconditionally calls `vscode.lm.registerTool('renderMermaidDiagram', ...)` in `activate()`, hitting the race on all platforms (Linux/Mac/Windows/Web). Fixes microsoft/vscode#326643 Recommended reviewer: `@bhavyaus` ### Culprit Commit Not identified from source — the repository checkout is a shallow clone (fetch-depth 1), so `git blame`/history for the phase divergence between `ChatExtensionPointHandler` (`BlockStartup`) and `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler` (`BlockRestore`) could not be traced. The issue is flagged `recent-regression`, consistent with the tools handler's phase being changed (or the handler being split out) more recently than the participants handler. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Extension activates
mermaid-markdown-features.activate] --> B[vscode.lm.registerTool
'renderMermaidDiagram'] B --> C[extHost: registerTool
_proxy.$registerTool id] C --> D[mainThread: $registerTool] D --> E[LanguageModelToolsService.registerToolImplementation id] E --> F{_tools.has id ?} F -- no --> G[throw Error
'Tool id was not contributed.'] F -- yes --> H[attach impl] I[LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler
WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore] -. registers tool DATA too late .-> F ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts` — registration phase of `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler`. Related (unchanged, for context): - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/languageModelToolsContribution.ts` — the extension-point handler that registers tool data from `package.json`. - `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts` (`$registerTool`) and `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts` (`registerToolImplementation`, throw site). - `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/src/chatOutputRenderer.ts` / `package.json` — the tool that surfaced the race. ### Repro Steps 1. Have a window where the `mermaid-markdown-features` extension activates early via a non-tool path (open a Markdown preview containing a mermaid block, or restore a window with a mermaid webview panel). 2. If the extension's `activate()` (and its `vscode.lm.registerTool('renderMermaidDiagram', ...)` call) runs before `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler` has installed its extension-point handler, the main thread throws `Tool "renderMermaidDiagram" was not contributed.` into error telemetry. Note: this is an activation-ordering race, so it reproduces intermittently depending on extension activation timing relative to workbench-contribution instantiation. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts`: register `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler` at `WorkbenchPhase.BlockStartup` instead of `WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore`. This mirrors the sibling `ChatExtensionPointHandler`, which already registers at `BlockStartup`. `BlockStartup` (`LifecyclePhase.Starting`) runs before extensions begin activating, so the extension-point handler's `setHandler` is installed — and all contributed tool data replayed and registered — before any extension can call `$registerTool`. The fix addresses the data *producer*'s ordering rather than guarding or swallowing at the throw site: `registerToolImplementation` still throws for genuinely un-contributed tools (e.g. typos), preserving the telemetry signal. The contribution's constructor only depends on `IProductService` and `ILanguageModelToolsService`, both available at startup, so moving the phase earlier is safe. **Alternatives considered:** - Deferring/queuing the implementation registration in `$registerTool` until the data is contributed — rejected because it would hide genuinely missing contributions (typos) and mask the error the throw is meant to surface, rather than fixing the ordering that produces the bad state. - Catching the fire-and-forget RPC error in the extension — rejected because it swallows the error at the consumer/crash site and hides it from telemetry. ### Recommended Owner `@bhavyaus` — active owner in the language-model tools area (e.g. main-thread tool-source handling in `$registerToolWithDefinition`, commit 9a1fe57), which is the subsystem affected here. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29756654207) · 2.2K AIC · ⌖ 35.1 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: don't stream chat progress into a completed response (fixes #326647)
body:
### Summary For contributed/streamed chat sessions (e.g. Copilot cloud sessions), `ChatServiceImpl` runs a single `autorun` that mirrors a provider-supplied `progressObs` into the model via `model.acceptResponseProgress(...)`. When the provider's observable emits additional progress items **after** the response has already been completed (progress and completion delivered on separate ticks), the autorun forwards them into an already-completed `ChatResponseModel`, which throws `acceptResponseProgress: Adding progress to a completed response`. The throw surfaces as an unhandled error in the Agents (`sessions`) window. Impact is a noisy uncaught error (158 hits / 109 users in 1.129.1) with no user-facing recovery. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326647 Recommended reviewer: `@osortega` ### Culprit Commit The bucket has non-zero hits in every tracked release (1.128.0, 1.128.1, 1.129.0, 1.129.1, 1.130.0-insider), first seen 2026-07-08. The underlying streaming autorun that forwards provider progress predates all of these, so this is a **pre-existing** consumer-side lifecycle bug rather than a single-commit regression. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | Hits appear in every release the bucket-history tool returns; the throwing code path (streaming `progressObs` into the model) predates the regression window. The large 1.129.x spike correlates with broader cloud/agent-host session rollout — notably [`3eb10e18`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3eb10e18b3f7c42ea4fbf4ef455f9e089c070032) (mid-turn steering, #325368), which reset progress tracking mid-stream and increased the chance progress arrives around completion — but that commit post-dates the first sighting, so it is a contributor to volume, not the introducer. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Provider as Contributed session (progressObs) participant Autorun as ChatServiceImpl autorun participant Model as ChatModel participant Response as ChatResponseModel Provider->>Autorun: isComplete = true (tick A) Autorun->>Model: completeLastResponse() Model->>Response: complete() → isComplete = true Note over Provider: ⚠️ Root cause:
progressObs appends more items after completion Provider->>Autorun: progressArray grows (tick B) Autorun->>Model: acceptResponseProgress(lastRequest, progress) Model->>Response: isComplete === true Note over Response: 💥 Error thrown:
Adding progress to a completed response ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatModel.ts` | crash site | L2992-2993: `if (request.response.isComplete) { throw new Error('acceptResponseProgress: Adding progress to a completed response'); }` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts` | root cause (consumer) | L987-990: `if (lastRequest && progressArray.length > lastProgressLength) { ... model?.acceptResponseProgress(lastRequest, progress); }` — forwards new progress without checking whether the response was already completed at L999 (`completeLastResponse()`) on a prior tick | ### Repro Steps 1. Open the Agents window with a contributed streamed session (e.g. a Copilot cloud session) that exposes `progressObs` + `isCompleteObs`. 2. Have the provider signal completion (`isCompleteObs` → true) on one observable tick, so the autorun calls `completeLastResponse()` and the `ChatResponseModel` becomes complete. 3. Have the same provider append one more progress item to `progressObs` on a subsequent tick (late/trailing chunk after the completion signal). 4. The streaming autorun forwards the trailing item via `acceptResponseProgress`, which throws because the response is already complete. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts`: guard the progress-forwarding loop with `!lastRequest.response?.isComplete` so trailing progress emitted after the response has been completed is dropped instead of being pushed into a completed `ChatResponseModel`. This is a consumer-side guard, which is the correct place here because the producer is an **extension-contributed observable** (`providedSession.progressObs`) — an external boundary whose emit ordering (progress after completion) the core cannot control or fix at its source. The guard does not mask a core-owned producer bug and does not use try/catch: the throwing telemetry path in `chatModel.ts` is preserved for every other caller. Within the same autorun tick where completion first occurs, `response.isComplete` is still `false` when the loop runs (completion happens later at L999), so legitimate final progress delivered alongside the completion signal is still accepted — only strictly-after-completion trailing items are skipped. **Alternatives considered:** - Wrap the `acceptResponseProgress` call in try/catch — rejected: hides the error from the telemetry pipeline instead of preventing the invalid state, and would swallow genuine misuse from other callers. - Widen `acceptResponseProgress` in `chatModel.ts` to silently no-op when complete — rejected: that patches the shared crash-site utility for all ~30 callers and removes a useful invariant check; the offending caller is the streaming autorun, so the fix belongs there. ### Recommended Owner `@osortega` — most recent author of the contributed-session progress-streaming / mid-turn-steering code in `chatServiceImpl.ts` (#325368) and actively working in this area. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29756691375) · 1.6K AIC · ⌖ 34.8 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- ### errors-fix-driver — cycle 1 **Trigger**: cron_review_comments · **Head**: `8baa98525235012264a6ddbf5bcaf19f3c6d7dca` (`8baa985`) + review-fix commit pushed this cycle | Item | Action | |------|--------| | Review on `chatServiceImpl.ts:990` (in scope) | Fixed — made response-exists check explicit (`lastRequest.response && !lastRequest.response.isComplete`); title: fix: skip null drag entries during file upload (fixes #326644)
body:
### Summary

`TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name')` is thrown when dropping content onto the File Explorer that is not a file-system entry (e.g. dragged text, a URL, or non-file drag data). `BrowserFileUpload.doUpload` builds an `entries` array from `DataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry()`, but that DOM API returns `FileSystemEntry | null` — it returns `null` for items that do not represent a file. The local `IWebkitDataTransferItem` interface incorrectly declared the return type as non-nullable, so the `null` was pushed into an array typed as `IWebkitDataTransferItemEntry[]`. Later, the parallel upload callback reads `entry.name` (the `factory` frame in the stack) and crashes on the `null` element.

This is a type-contract violation: the interface lied about the return type, letting a `null` bypass the type system at the producer (the array-building loop), and the crash surfaced far downstream at `entry.name`.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326644
Recommended reviewer: `@bpasero`

### Culprit Commit

The masking type declaration (`webkitGetAsEntry(): IWebkitDataTransferItemEntry`) and the `entries.push(item.webkitGetAsEntry())` producer are long-standing in `fileImportExport.ts` (the browser upload feature authored by `@bpasero`). No single recent commit introduced the null path; the telemetry `recent-regression`/`stable-anomaly` signals reflect a change in drop-input mix rather than a code change to this file. Most recent touch to the file was `7e8c7bef` ("debt - reduce explicit `any` usage", `@bpasero`), which did not alter this behavior.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[HTMLDivElement drop handler] --> B[ExplorerDelegate.drop]
    B --> C[BrowserFileUpload.upload -> withProgress]
    C --> D[doUpload: entries.push webkitGetAsEntry]
    D -->|API returns null for non-file item| E[null pushed into entries array]
    E --> F[Limiter.queue callback / factory]
    F --> G[read entry.name on null -> TypeError]
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/fileImportExport.ts` — fix the `IWebkitDataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry` return type and skip `null` entries when building the upload list.

### Repro Steps

1. Open a folder in VS Code (desktop or web).
2. Drag non-file content (e.g. selected text from a web page, or a URL) onto the File Explorer and drop it.
3. `webkitGetAsEntry()` returns `null` for that item; before the fix, `doUpload` pushed the `null` and later read `entry.name`, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name')`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/fileImportExport.ts`):

- Corrected the `IWebkitDataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry` return type to `IWebkitDataTransferItemEntry | null`, matching the real DOM contract. This removes the type-system bypass that allowed `null` to enter a non-nullable array.
- In `doUpload`, the array-building loop now captures the result and only pushes it when it is non-`null`, so `entries` never contains a `null`. This fixes the bug at the data producer (where the invalid `null` is created) rather than guarding the crash site (`entry.name`), consistent with the fix-at-the-producer principle. No `try/catch` is added and no `logService.error` is touched.

After this change, the `doUpload` loop cannot place a `null` into `entries`, so the downstream `entry.name` read can no longer receive a `null` element.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Guarding `entry.name` at the crash site (line 166 / the `factory` callback) — rejected because it patches the symptom downstream and leaves the mistyped interface producing `null` for every other consumer.

### Recommended Owner

`@bpasero` — original author of the browser file upload/import-export feature and most recent committer to this file.

title: Batch action list width measurements
body:
## Summary

- batch action-list row width writes, geometry reads, and restores into three phases
- preserve the row-to-item mapping used for toolbar-width accounting in visible and temporarily expanded hidden-item paths
- add regression coverage for measurement ordering, toolbar accounting, and width restoration

## Performance

Chromium CDP instrumentation over 49 representative rows and 200 measurement passes:

| Implementation | Layouts | Style recalculations | Duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Alternating write/read/write | 9,801 | 9,801 | 110.2 ms |
| Batched write/read/write | 2 | 201 | 7.5 ms |

Measured row widths were identical.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client -- --pretty false`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`

Fixes #326640

cc @sandy081

title: Batch ListView horizontal width measurement
body:
## Summary

- batch horizontal row width measurement into write, read, and reset phases
- apply batching to visible-row insertion, range scrolling, and runtime horizontal-scrolling enablement
- preserve per-row padding calculations, width caching, and deferred scroll-width updates

The dynamic-height probe remains separate; `ListView` rejects combining dynamic heights with horizontal scrolling.

## Verification

- added a deterministic `ListView` test proving all five `fit-content` writes precede all five `offsetWidth` reads for splice, scroll/reuse, and enablement paths
- verified per-row padding arithmetic and row-width resets
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted `ListView` unit suite
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- staged pre-commit hygiene

title: fix: cap Claude session workspace changes to prevent RPC serialization overflow (fixes #326633)
body:
### Summary

Telemetry bucket `e13f00b3-4c2d-4070-7b5b-c2be62d17389` reports `RangeError: Invalid string length` thrown from `JSON.stringify` inside the extension-host RPC layer (`serializeRequestArguments` → `_remoteCall` in `rpcProtocol.ts`). The originating call is `x2e._refreshItems`, which maps to `_refreshItems` in `claudeChatSessionContentProvider.ts`. That method builds the full `vscode.ChatSessionItem[]` collection and hands it to `this._controller.items.replace(items)`, serializing the entire collection across the extension-host boundary in a single `JSON.stringify` call.

Each item carries a `changes` array produced by `ClaudeWorkspaceFolderService`. That array is **unbounded**: it is derived directly from a git diff and, for a pathological repository state (e.g. a large untracked directory such as `node_modules` staged into the temporary index), can contain hundreds of thousands of `ChatSessionChangedFile` entries. Serialized in bulk across all sessions, the resulting JSON string exceeds V8's maximum string length (~2^29 chars), throwing `RangeError: Invalid string length`. This is a resource-exhaustion error (not a type-contract violation), and it is consistent with the `recent-regression` label — the workspace-changes enrichment was added recently in PR #312043.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326633
Recommended reviewer: `@TylerLeonhardt`

### Culprit Commit

`b88dca159c0b8ced67a7cd3371005aa76e48cb00` — "feat(claude): implement workspace folder service for tracking file changes in chat sessions (#312043)" by `@TylerLeonhardt` (2026-04-23). This commit introduced `ClaudeWorkspaceFolderService`, which produces the unbounded `changes` array that is later serialized across RPC. (History was not directly walkable in the shallow CI checkout; the culprit was located via the GitHub commit API for the affected file.)

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[git diff in ClaudeWorkspaceFolderService.computeRepositoryChanges] --> B[unbounded result.changes array]
    B --> C[_computeAndCacheChanges maps to ChatSessionChangedFile array]
    C --> D[_createClaudeChatSessionItem sets item.changes]
    D --> E[_refreshItems builds ChatSessionItem collection]
    E --> F[controller.items.replace items]
    F --> G[rpcProtocol serializeRequestArguments JSON.stringify]
    G --> H[RangeError: Invalid string length]
```

### Affected Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/claudeWorkspaceFolderServiceImpl.ts` — producer of the unbounded `changes` array (fixed here).
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/claudeChatSessionContentProvider.ts` — `_refreshItems` / `_createClaudeChatSessionItem` consume `changes` and trigger serialization (not modified).
- `src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/rpcProtocol.ts` — core RPC boundary where `JSON.stringify` throws (crash site, deliberately not modified).

### Repro Steps

1. Open a workspace whose git working tree has an extremely large number of changed/untracked files (e.g. a big generated or `node_modules`-style directory that ends up staged into the temporary diff index).
2. Open the Agents App so Claude chat sessions are enumerated.
3. `ClaudeWorkspaceFolderService` computes a `changes` array with hundreds of thousands of entries per session.
4. `_refreshItems` calls `items.replace(...)`, serializing the collection over RPC → `RangeError: Invalid string length`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `claudeWorkspaceFolderServiceImpl.ts`: cap the `changes` list at its producer. A new `MAX_CHANGES_PER_SESSION = 1000` constant bounds the array in `_computeAndCacheChanges` before it is mapped into `ChatSessionChangedFile` objects and cached. When the raw diff exceeds the cap, we emit `this._logService.warn(...)` (preserving observability) and slice to the cap. This fixes the problem at the data producer rather than the crash site: the oversized object graph can no longer be constructed, so the downstream RPC `JSON.stringify` cannot overflow. A per-session cap of 1000 is far beyond what the Sessions/Changes view can meaningfully present, so there is no practical loss of information.

This deliberately does **not** wrap the `JSON.stringify` crash site in `try/catch` (that would hide the error from telemetry without fixing the cause) and does **not** remove any `logService.error` calls.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Guarding/try-catching at `rpcProtocol.ts` `serializeRequestArguments` — rejected: it masks the symptom at the crash site and would silently drop the entire RPC payload for all callers, not just this one.
- Truncating in `_refreshItems` (the consumer) — rejected: the oversized array is still built and cached upstream, and other consumers of the service would remain exposed; the correct place is the data producer.

### Recommended Owner

`@TylerLeonhardt` — authored `ClaudeWorkspaceFolderService` (PR #312043, commit `b88dca1`) which introduced the unbounded `changes` producer, and is an active VS Code team member with recent commits in this area.

title: fix: translate notebook range to alt-cell index space in alternativeNotebookTextDocument (fixes #326632)
body:
### Summary `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startOffset')` thrown from `withNotebookChangesAndEdit` in the Copilot Chat extension's `alternativeNotebookTextDocument.ts` (deminified frame `../src/platform/notebook/common/alternativeNotebookTextDocument.ts:398:93`, reached via `toAltNotebookChangeEdit` / `applyNotebookChanges` from an `onDidChangeNotebookDocument` handler). Root cause: `event.range` on a notebook content change is expressed in the notebook's **full cell index space** (including markdown cells), but the alternative document's `altCells` array **excludes markdown cells** when `excludeMarkdownCells` is `true` (the default used by the inline-edits workspace). When markdown cells precede the changed range, `event.range.start` is larger than `altCells.length`, so `altCells[event.range.start - 1]` is `undefined` and reading `.startOffset` throws. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326632 Recommended reviewer: `@DonJayamanne` ### Culprit Commit Could not identify the exact introducing commit — the CI checkout is a shallow (grafted) clone with no history for this file, and commit search returned no hits. The bug lives in the index math of `withNotebookChangesAndEdit`; the redundant identical `if (event.range.isEmpty) { ... } else { ... }` branch that computed `firstUnChangedCellIndex` is a strong signal of a recent refactor in this area. Marked `recent-regression` on the issue. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[VS Code: onDidChangeNotebookDocument] -->|e.contentChanges
range in full notebook index space| B[vscodeWorkspace.ts
applyNotebookChanges / toAltNotebookChangeEdit] B --> C[withNotebookChangesAndEdit
altCells excludes markdown cells] C --> D["firstUnChangedCellIndex = range.start - 1"] D --> E["altCells[firstUnChangedCellIndex]
index > altCells.length -> undefined"] E --> F["read .startOffset -> TypeError"] ``` ### Affected Files - `extensions/copilot/src/platform/notebook/common/alternativeNotebookTextDocument.ts` — `withNotebookChangesAndEdit` indexed/sliced/spliced the filtered `altCells` array with unfiltered notebook `event.range` values. ### Repro Steps 1. Open a notebook whose leading cells are markdown, followed by a code cell (e.g. `[markdown, markdown, code]`). 2. With Copilot inline edits (alternative notebook format, `excludeMarkdownCells = true`) active, insert or remove a code cell at a notebook index that is `> number of code cells` (e.g. append a code cell at notebook index 3 while only one code cell exists). 3. The `onDidChangeNotebookDocument` handler calls `applyNotebookChanges`; `altCells[event.range.start - 1]` is `undefined` and `.startOffset` throws. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`alternativeNotebookTextDocument.ts`): translate `event.range` from the notebook's full cell index space into the `altCells` index space **before** indexing, slicing, or splicing. Each `AltCellInfo` already carries its underlying `NotebookCell` (`altCell.cell.index`), so the translated bounds are computed as the number of `altCells` whose notebook `index` falls before the range endpoints: ```ts const altRangeStart = altCells.filter(c => c.altCell.cell.index < event.range.start).length; const altRangeEnd = altCells.filter(c => c.altCell.cell.index < event.range.end).length; ``` All subsequent uses (`removedCells` slice, `firstUnChangedCellIndex`, the "cells after the range" checks, and the final `splice`) now use `altRangeStart`/`altRangeEnd`. This fixes the bug at the **data producer** (where notebook-space indices are consumed against a filtered array) rather than guarding the crash site. With this change, `firstUnChangedCellIndex` is always `≤ altCells.length - 1`, so `altCells[firstUnChangedCellIndex]` can no longer be `undefined` — the `TypeError` cannot be produced. The redundant identical `if/else` computing `firstUnChangedCellIndex` was collapsed in the process. title: fix: guard undefined cursor range in NES cache lookup (fixes #326631)
body:
### Summary

`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'start')` fires from `OffsetRange.containsRange` when the Next Edit Suggestion (NES) cache is looked up with an empty selection. In `DocumentEditCache.lookupNextEdit`, `cursorRange` is read as `currentSelection[0]`; when the selection array is empty this is `undefined`, and the cursor-jump window check then calls `editWindow.containsRange(undefined)` / `originalEditWindow.containsRange(undefined)`, which dereferences `undefined.start` in core.

The same function already guards `cursorRange` before its later cursor-distance check (`&& cursorRange`), but the cursor-jump window check added for the jump-target/original-window feature did not. The fix restores that guard at the producer of the `undefined` value, so an empty selection yields a cache miss instead of a crash.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326631
Recommended reviewer: `@chrmarti`

### Culprit Commit

Not identified by hash — the `extensions/copilot` sources are a vendored snapshot in `microsoft/vscode` and this repo checkout is shallow (no usable git history), and GitHub commit/PR search returned no matches for the cursor-jump code. The regression was introduced by the cursor-jump NES feature that added the `originalEditWindow` window check (lines 337–341 of `nextEditCache.ts`), which called `containsRange(cursorRange)` without the `cursorRange !== undefined` guard the neighbouring cursor-distance block already uses. Issue carries the `recent-regression` label, consistent with this recently added feature.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[provideInlineCompletionItems] --> B[NextEditProvider.getNextEdit]
    B --> C[_getNextEditCanThrow]
    C --> D[NextEditCache.lookupNextEdit]
    D --> E[DocumentEditCache.lookupNextEdit]
    E --> F["cursorRange = currentSelection[0] (undefined when selection empty)"]
    F --> G["editWindow?.containsRange(cursorRange)"]
    G --> H["OffsetRange.containsRange reads other.start on undefined"]
    H --> I["TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'start')"]
```

### Affected Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditCache.ts` — `DocumentEditCache.lookupNextEdit`, cursor-jump window containment check.

### Repro Steps

1. Have an NES cache entry with an `editWindow` (cursor-jump edit) for the active document.
2. Trigger an inline-completion request while `currentSelection` is empty (no selection/cursor range supplied), so `currentSelection[0]` is `undefined`.
3. `lookupNextEdit` calls `editWindow.containsRange(undefined)` → `TypeError` reading `start`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`nextEditCache.ts`): guard the two cursor-jump window checks with `cursorRange !== undefined` before invoking `containsRange`:

```ts
const inEditWindow = cursorRange !== undefined && editWindow?.containsRange(cursorRange);
const inOriginalWindow = cursorRange !== undefined && originalEditWindow?.containsRange(cursorRange);
```

This fixes the data producer, not the crash site: the `undefined` originates from `currentSelection[0]` in this function, so the guard belongs here rather than inside core's `OffsetRange.containsRange` (a widely-used typed utility that must not absorb invalid input). When `cursorRange` is `undefined` both flags are `false`, so `if (editWindow && !inEditWindow && !inOriginalWindow)` returns `undefined` — a clean cache miss (no suggestion) instead of a thrown error, which is strictly safer than the previous crash and consistent with the existing `&& cursorRange` guard used a few lines below for the cursor-distance check. Core's `containsRange` is left unchanged and continues to enforce its non-nullable `OffsetRange` contract.

**Alternatives considered**: adding a guard inside `OffsetRange.containsRange` — rejected because it would let a shared typed utility silently accept `undefined`, masking future producers of bad data; wrapping the lookup in try/catch — rejected because it hides the error from telemetry rather than fixing the empty-selection producer.

### Recommended Owner

`@chrmarti` — owns the NES cache code (active `TODO@chrmarti` in `lookupNextEdit`) and the inline-edits cursor-jump feature area.

title: NES: split open-tab vs related-file neighbor context

labels.name: release-cherry-pick
labels.description: Automated cherry-pick between release and main branches

body:
## Summary

Two related improvements to the **xtab (NES / Next Edit Suggestions)** *neighboring-files context*. Both hinge on distinguishing neighbor snippets that come from **open tabs** vs. from **language-service "related" files** (the non-open-tab files a language service suggests, e.g. `related/typescript`, `related/cpp`).

1. **No line numbers for related-file snippets.** Snippets sourced from language-service related files now omit line numbers in the prompt, matching NES's *own* language-context path (`appendLanguageContextSnippets`, which already uses `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None`). Open-tab neighbor snippets are unchanged and keep their line numbers.
2. **Ability to turn off the related-files context.** A new `neighborFiles.includeRelatedFiles` option lets us disable the completions-style related-files context entirely, since NES already has its own language-context implementation (`ILanguageContextProviderService`). When off, the related-files LSP computation is **skipped entirely** (no wasted work), leaving only open-tab neighbors.

Both default to **behavior-preserving** settings, so this PR is a no-op until the new config is flipped.

## Motivation

NES's neighboring-files context (Jaccard-ranked snippets from Completions) overlaps with NES's own language context. This PR makes the two coexist cleanly: related-file snippets are formatted consistently with the language-context path (no line numbers), and the redundant related-files context can be switched off per experiment.

## What changed

**Point 1 — provenance tag + line-number formatting.** Each neighbor snippet carries its provenance, decided once at the source (where the neighbor type is known) rather than re-derived from URIs:
- `neighborFiles.ts` (completions-core): `isRelatedNeighboringFileType(type)` is a `switch` over the `Related*` enum members (robust to enum changes, no string-prefix matching). `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` stamps `isFromRelatedFile` on each related doc as it is materialized.
- `prompt.ts` / `selectRelevance.ts`: `SimilarFileInfo` and `ScoredSnippet` gain an optional `isFromRelatedFile`. `getSimilarSnippets` propagates it (and the source `uri`) onto every ranked snippet and guarantees it on its return type (`SnippetWithSourceInfo`).
- `similarFilesContext.ts`: `getSnippetsForPrompt` reads `s.isFromRelatedFile` directly — no post-ranking URI set / cross-referencing.
- `similarFilesContextService.ts`: `INeighborFileSnippet` gains `readonly isFromRelatedFile: boolean`.
- `recentFilesForPrompt.ts`: `appendNeighborFileSnippets` uses `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None` for related-file snippets, else the configured option.

**Point 2 — toggle**
- `xtabPromptOptions.ts`: adds `includeRelatedFiles` to `NeighborFilesOptions` (type + `VALIDATOR` + `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, default `true`).
- `configurationService.ts`: new team-internal, experiment-based key `chat.advanced.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.neighborFiles.includeRelatedFiles`.
- `xtabProvider.ts`: wires the config into the `neighborFiles` options and threads the flag into `getSnippetsForPrompt` and the fire-and-forget telemetry `compute`.
- `neighborFiles.ts` (completions-core): `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` gains an `includeRelatedFiles: boolean = true` param; when `false` it returns early with open-tab neighbors only, before any related-files/LSP work.

## Behavior & compatibility

- **Defaults unchanged:** `includeRelatedFiles` defaults to `true`; related files continue to be included exactly as before. Line-numbering for open-tab snippets is unchanged.
- **Only new behavior** is (a) related-file snippets drop line numbers, and (b) the new exp key can turn related files off.
- Gated correctly for AI-disabled users — this is inside the existing xtab provider path and only runs when `neighborFiles.enabled` is on.

## How to review

Suggested reading order:

1. **`similarFilesContextService.ts`** — the new `isFromRelatedFile` field + the `includeRelatedFiles` param on the two service methods. This is the contract for everything else.
2. **`neighborFiles.ts`** (completions-core) — `isRelatedNeighboringFileType`, the `isFromRelatedFile` stamp on related docs, and the one-line early-return in `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` (`if (!includeRelatedFiles || featuresService.excludeRelatedFiles(...))`). Confirm skipping related files still returns open-tab neighbors + empty traits.
3. **`similarFiles.ts` / `selectRelevance.ts`** — the tag rides on `SimilarFileInfo` → each snippet; `getSimilarSnippets` guarantees `uri` + `isFromRelatedFile` on its return type.
4. **`similarFilesContext.ts`** — `getSnippetsForPrompt` classifies purely from `s.isFromRelatedFile` (no URI set), so multi-root relative-path collisions can't misclassify a snippet.
5. **`recentFilesForPrompt.ts`** — related snippets get `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None`; open-tab snippets keep the configured option.

## Tests

- `similarFiles.test.ts` (prompt): `getSimilarSnippets` preserves each source `uri` under a multi-root relativePath collision, and propagates `isFromRelatedFile` from source file → snippet.
- `neighborFiles.test.ts` (completions-core): `includeRelatedFiles=false` retains open-tab neighbors, keeps traits empty, and (via a call counter on the mocked provider) proves the related-files provider is never invoked — with a positive control for the enabled path.
- `recentFilesForPrompt.spec.ts` (xtab): related snippets omit line numbers; open-tab snippets keep them.
